issues.description: The problem statement requires implementing init_world(width, height) to set both dimensions, but the solution's init_world only reads one parameter (width) and ignores height. This mismatch can confuse students about the required function signature and expected behavior: they will implement a two-parameter init_world as specified, while the reference solution demonstrates handling only a single parameter.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the artifacts consistent. Either (A) update the solution's init_world to accept and handle both width and height (e.g., read width from [esp+4] and height from [esp+8], and store/use both as required by the exercise), or (B) if only width is intended, update the problem statement to specify init_world(width) (single parameter). Preferred fix: implement proper two-parameter handling in solution so it matches the problem statement (and, if useful, add a stub for init_world in the template to guide students).
